questions.question: On a number line, you want to estimate 47 + 38. Round each number to the nearest ten. What is your estimate?
questions.explain: Round 47 up to 50 and 38 down to 40, then add: 50 + 40 = 90. The trap is rounding 47 down to 40 or giving the exact answer 85 instead of an estimate.

questions.question: On a number line, you want to estimate 263 − 87. Round each to the nearest ten. What is your estimate?
questions.explain: Round 263 down to 260 and 87 up to 90, then subtract: 260 − 90 = 170. Watch out for rounding 87 down to 80 or giving the exact answer 176.

questions.question: On a number line, you want to estimate 512 + 278. Round each to the nearest hundred. What is your estimate?
questions.explain: Round 512 down to 500 and 278 up to 300, then add: 500 + 300 = 800. The trap is rounding 278 down to 200 instead of up to 300.

questions.question: On a number line, you want to estimate 435 − 189. Round each to the nearest hundred. What is your estimate?
questions.explain: Round 435 down to 400 and 189 up to 200, then subtract: 400 − 200 = 200. Watch out for rounding 189 down to 100 or giving the exact answer 246.

questions.question: Ben computes 483 + 291 = 774. His estimate is 500 + 300 = 800. What should Ben think?
options: 774 is close to 800, so it looks right
774 must be 800, so it is wrong
774 is fine, the estimate is not needed
The estimate is 700, so 774 is wrong
questions.explain: 774 is close to the estimate of 800, so the answer looks reasonable. An estimate is not the exact answer, so it is fine that the two numbers are not the same.

questions.question: A child estimates 347 + 256 as 350 + 260 = 610. She computes and gets 98. What should she do?
options: 98 is close enough to 610, so it is fine
98 is far from 610, so she should recheck
98 must equal 610, so it is wrong
256 rounds to 200, so the estimate is 550
questions.explain: 98 is very far from the estimate of 610, so the child should recheck her work. A good estimate helps you spot a big mistake right away.

questions.question: A child estimates 248 + 176 as 250 + 200 = 450. She computes and gets 424. What does the estimate tell her?
options: 424 must equal 450, so it is wrong
424 is fine, the estimate is not needed
424 is close to 450, so it looks right
176 rounds to 100, so the estimate is 350
questions.explain: 424 is close to the estimate of 450, so the answer looks right. The estimate is a rough check, not the exact answer you must get.

questions.question: A child estimates 862 − 347 as 900 − 300 = 600. She computes and gets 109. What should she think?
options: 109 is fine, the estimate is just a guess
109 must be exactly 600, so it is wrong
862 rounds to 800, so the estimate is 500
109 is far from 600, so it has a mistake
questions.explain: 109 is very far from the estimate of 600, so something is wrong with the computation. Use the estimate as a quick check to catch big errors.

questions.question: A child estimates 478 + 293 − 156. She rounds to 500 + 300 − 200 = 600. She computes 771 − 156 = 615. What does the estimate tell her?
options: 615 is close to 600, so it looks right
615 must be 600, so it is wrong
615 is fine, the estimate is not needed
293 rounds to 200, so the total is 500
questions.explain: 615 is close to the estimate of 600, so the answer looks reasonable. Rounding 293 down to 200 would give a wrong estimate of 500.

questions.question: A child writes: 'I estimated 634 + 287 as 600 + 300 = 900. I computed 921. 921 is not 900, so my answer is wrong.' What is the mistake in this thinking?
options: 634 rounds to 700, not 600
The estimate need not be exact
The estimate is not needed at all
287 rounds to 400, not 300
questions.explain: The estimate of 900 and the answer of 921 are close, so the answer is fine. The mistake is thinking the answer must equal the estimate exactly.

questions.question: A child has 543 marbles. She gives away 268 and estimates 500 − 300 = 200. She counts the rest and gets 87. Is her count reasonable?
options: 87 is close enough to 200, so it is fine
87 must be exactly 200, so it is wrong
87 is far from 200, so count them again
268 rounds to 200, so the estimate is 300
questions.explain: 87 is far from the estimate of 200, so the child should count the marbles again. A good estimate helps you notice when your count is way off.

questions.question: A child estimates 725 + 194 as 700 + 200 = 900. She has three possible answers: 919, 1924, and 531. Which one should she pick?
options: None, because 725 should round to 800
1924, because it is bigger than 900
531, because it must equal 900 exactly
919, because it is close to 900
questions.explain: 919 is close to the estimate of 900, so it is the reasonable answer. 1924 and 531 are both too far from 900 to be right.
